_source: README Expected outcomes — E2E-29, CAPABILITY form (mergewatch.ai#570, option 2). This used to assert `mustContain: "Related concerns clustered into this finding"`. The literal is stable product boilerplate, but whether it is EMITTED depends on the model producing findings that overlap enough for W10 to merge — which is exactly the model judgement the old note claimed it avoided. It failed the deploy gate on a change that could not affect it (a YAML permissions block), blocking production and costing a full suite to re-run. Asserted now is what the PR surface can observe deterministically: the review ran on a file built to draw several overlapping concerns in one region, and produced at least one critical. `critical: {min: 1}` is one-sided, so it cannot fail because the model found MORE than expected — which is why the `declare const` confound that broke 22-claim-aware-verify is deliberately left in place here: removing it would produce FEWER findings and make clustering less likely, the opposite of what this fixture needs. The clustering render itself — the audit-trail block, the '… and N related concern(s)' title, the strongest-severity rule, and the `[clustering] merged N` agent log — stays in the README's expected outcomes as a manual check. The agent log is not visible from the PR surface at all, so no automated assertion could have covered the capability directly.
